title: Introduce tenant probation fuse and regional stability probe
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: we observed tenant churn and cascading regional rejoin oscillations during a partial-e2 region degradation in staging; this caused repeated KV cache warm drains and SLO spikes. This PR introduces a tenant probation fuse component (lightweight, in-server token-bucket-like probation state) combined with a region stability probe that informs the probation time constants. The goal is to reduce rapid tenant re-admittance and prevent repeated warm-drain cycles while keeping degradation observable and reversible. Design summary: probation_fuse is implemented as a compact Rust module in the runtime that tags tenant sessions with a probation score and an exponential decay window; the probe (Go) runs as an opt-in controller per-region and emits a stability score via the control plane; routing picks up the score and raises probation thresholds when region instability is detected. Key changes: runtime admission logic, a small control-loop probe, telemetry counters and histograms, integration test harness, and a helm values toggle for staged rollout. Testing: unit tests for probation decay and admission thresholds; integration harness simulates rapid tenant disconnect/rejoin and confirms a ~40% reduction in warm-drain events; manual canary in staging passed for 24h. Rollout plan: enable feature-flag off by default, enable for 10% of tenants in staging for 24h, then ramp to 100% in region beta if no regressions. Rollback: flip helm flag to false or revert main config; probation state expires naturally. Checklist: [x] unit tests; [x] integration test; [x] metrics and tracing; [x] docs and helm values; [x] staging canary. Related: ENG-4123 for telemetry work, SUP-889 for incident context.
